Narrow scope limited to 4 material types; other important phenomena (rigid body dynamics, fractures, deformable objects beyond cloth) are absent, limiting comprehensiveness

Physically grounded dataset construction with careful solver selection, parameter tuning, and high-quality rendering (path tracing, 256 samples/pixel) at 640×720 resolution

Insufficient guidance for future research. While identifying method failures, the paper lacks concrete direction on what alternative representations or approaches should be developed to solve identified problems
Ground-truth particle trajectories provided but not leveraged—no baseline methods demonstrate how to utilize this information for physics-aware modeling, representing missed opportunity
Physical realism unvalidated: While using physics solvers, paper lacks validation that outputs match real physics or comparison with actual footage of similar phenomena
Quantitative evaluation misaligned with claims: Uses PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS which don't measure physics accuracy (acknowledged but unresolved); no proposed metrics for evaluating physical realism
Monocular DyNVS claimed as contribution but minimally evaluated with limited analysis of monocular-specific challenges or performance
Missing experimental depth: No ablation studies on failure causes, no analysis of which scene properties challenge methods most, no difficulty calibration validation

Comprehensive dataset construction using established physics simulators (FLIP, Pyro, MPM, Vellum) with detailed documentation of parameters enabling reproducibility
Valuable analysis (Section 5.2) demonstrating fundamental limitation: RGB-based reconstruction fidelity alone does not guarantee physical realism—identified as key insight for future research
Systematic experimental evaluation of state-of-the-art methods with both quantitative metrics and qualitative analysis across multiple settings and materials
Excellent accessibility and reproducibility: detailed implementation specifications, customizable simulation graphs, and commitment to public release with comprehensive documentation
Supports diverse research configurations: both multiview and monocular setups, enabling broader applicability across DyNVS research directions
Clear presentation with effective visualizations demonstrating dataset capabilities and method failure modes on complex multi-body interactions
weaknesses: Limited methodological or algorithmic novelty; purely a dataset paper without proposed methods that leverage physics information
Modest dataset scale with only 17 scenes (4-5 per material category), potentially limiting statistical significance and generalization across scenarios
Restricted scope of physics phenomena: primarily simple scenarios (objects in containers) without complex multi-material mixing, long-term deformations, or naturalistic interactions
Synthetic-only data without real-world validation; sim-to-real gap is acknowledged in Appendix D but not addressed, limiting practical applicability
Incomplete evaluation of physics information utility: ground-truth parameters are provided but not rigorously evaluated for recoverability from images or downstream task performance
Analysis identifies limitations of existing methods but offers limited guidance on architectural solutions or how to design methods that leverage physics information
Limited demonstration of practical utility beyond standard reconstruction metrics; inverse parameter estimation and simulation prediction tasks not evaluated

strengths: Addresses a critical gap by introducing the first physics-aware benchmark for DyNVS with complex multi-body interactions, filling an important need in the community where existing datasets focus on single objects or materials

Comprehensive dataset with complete ground-truth physics information including 3D particle trajectories, physical parameters, and material-specific solver details across 4 material categories using rigorous physics simulation (FLIP, Pyro, MPM, Vellum)

Rigorous dual-metric evaluation framework that captures both photorealism (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) and physics accuracy (TD/AUOP), with per-scene breakdown and extensive comparison of 5 recent methods demonstrating clear performance gaps on physics realism
Excellent reproducibility with detailed technical specifications of physics solvers, parameters, camera configurations, rendering settings, and source code availability enabling future research
Clear demonstration of fundamental limitations in existing DyNVS methods regarding multi-body interactions and physics reasoning, with honest discussion of failure modes and their causes
Well-designed evaluation metrics (TD and AUOP) that intuitively capture trajectory alignment and robustness to outliers, complementing existing photorealism metrics
weaknesses: Limited scene scale and diversity with only 17 scenes (4-5 per material type) covering relatively simple, controlled scenarios with restricted material variation (e.g., single cloth type in textile category), raising questions about benchmark representativeness

Inherent limitations of synthetic-only data with physics simulations using simplified constitutive models and grid-based discretization; no validation against real-world physics measurements or quantification of the simulation-reality gap limits practical applicability

Primarily a dataset contribution without methodological novelty—no new rendering algorithms, physics-informed learning methods, or architectural innovations proposed; relies on straightforward application of existing rendering pipeline

Insufficient analysis of method failures providing limited insight into why methods fail beyond 'multi-body interactions are hard'; lacks ablation studies on necessary architectural components, oracle performance bounds, or systematic error mode analysis

Extremely high computational barrier to adoption with simulation times of 12-24 hours for complex scenes and expensive rendering; no discussion of approximations or simplified variants limits accessibility to researchers with limited computational resources

Incomplete physics coverage lacking rigid body contacts, deformable body interactions with complex contact dynamics, non-Newtonian fluids, and coupled physics phenomena; limited guidance on how to bridge the photorealism-physics accuracy gap

Modest scene scale and limited per-category complexity progression compared to major benchmarks; different camera configurations for different scene types (2 vs. 4 cameras) complicates cross-scene comparison and may affect method generalization

strengths: Addresses a genuine gap in DyNVS research by identifying the lack of physics-aware evaluation for multi-body interactions
Comprehensive material diversity with proper physics simulators (FLIP, Pyro, Vellum, MPM) tailored to different materials
Complete ground-truth provision including 3D particle trajectories and material-specific physics parameters
Introduces novel evaluation metrics (TD, AUOP) specifically targeting physical realism beyond photorealism
Strong reproducibility effort with source code, detailed solver specifications, and COLMAP point clouds provided
Extensive comparison of recent DyNVS methods revealing systematic limitations
weaknesses: Purely dataset/benchmark paper with no methodological contributions; doesn't propose methods to address identified challenges

Critical benchmark validation failure: all tested methods show catastrophically poor physics metrics (Table 6), and even Oracle baseline shows poor performance—raises fundamental questions about metric/benchmark calibration that are acknowledged but unresolved
Severely limited evaluation of proposed metrics: TD and AUOP only tested on 2 scenes despite being central contributions; Young's modulus estimates off by orders of magnitude (Table 7)
Small dataset size (17 scenes, 4-5 per material) insufficient for training modern deep learning models compared to existing benchmarks, with no augmentation strategies discussed
Acknowledged but unaddressed simulation-reality gap: uses simplified physics models (incompressible fluids, simplified rheological models) without validation against real-world physics
Incomplete technical analysis: lacks ablation studies, no investigation of what makes benchmark challenging, no guidance on improving methods or selecting approaches for material types
Trajectory Distance metric under-specified: unclear methodology for matching particles, vulnerable to identity swapping, requires manual annotation with insufficient detail
AUOP metric concerns: outlier threshold δ is ad-hoc and scene-dependent, only validated on 2 scenes, fundamental design appears flawed
Experimental setup inconsistencies: varying monoclular vs. 4-camera setups across scenes, uneven complexity distribution, some scenes (single_smoke) don't showcase multi-body interactions
Missing inverse physics evaluation: only 2 methods tested for physics parameter estimation, both fail dramatically, providing no insights for improvement

strengths: Addresses a critical gap in DyNVS research by introducing the first physics-aware benchmark with rigorous evaluation of multi-body interactions across diverse materials (liquids, gases, rheological substances, textiles)

Comprehensive dataset design with complete ground-truth information: 3D particle trajectories, material-specific physics parameters, and multiple camera configurations enabling diverse evaluation scenarios
Novel and well-justified evaluation metrics (Trajectory Distance and Area Under Outlier Percentage) specifically designed to measure physics plausibility rather than photorealism alone
Rigorous physics simulation using industry-standard solvers (FLIP, Pyro, MPM, Vellum) with carefully tuned parameters and detailed documentation of governing equations and physical assumptions
Extensive experimental analysis demonstrating clear limitations of existing SOTA methods on multi-body physics understanding, with per-scene breakdowns revealing method-specific failure modes
Exceptional reproducibility and accessibility: source code for physics solvers, COLMAP reconstruction points, customizable framework, and comprehensive parameter documentation in appendices
High-quality presentation with excellent visualizations effectively conveying scene complexity and method failures; well-organized structure bridging main paper and detailed appendices
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty beyond dataset creation; primarily a benchmarking contribution without novel algorithms, training strategies, or deep insights into solving physics-aware reconstruction

Insufficient validation of simulator physics accuracy: no perceptual studies or real-world comparison demonstrating that simulated dynamics match actual physical behavior, despite acknowledged simplifications in constitutive models

Weak demonstration of dataset utility: evaluates existing methods but lacks ablation studies, case studies of method development using PhysGaia, or evidence that the benchmark drives meaningful algorithmic improvements

Physics parameter estimation analysis (Section 5.3) is underdeveloped: Table 7 shows dramatic failures in Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio estimation but provides limited investigation into root causes or solutions

Limited exploration of failure modes: while Figures D-E show needle-like artifacts across all methods on multi-body scenarios, the paper offers insufficient analysis of whether this reflects fundamental Gaussian splatting limitations or other addressable issues
Modest scale and scope: 17 synthetic scenes may be insufficient compared to modern standards; entirely synthetic limits generalization claims; no evaluation on uncontrolled real-world captures

Missing computational and practical analysis: simulation times (12-24 hours) not contextualized within cost-benefit framework; unclear whether PhysGaia is preferable to collecting real-world sequences for practical applications

Incomplete investigation of camera configuration rationale: different scenes use 2 vs. 4 cameras without principled justification, potentially impacting reproducibility; limited analysis of how camera count affects physics understanding vs. photorealism
